findings.finding: The `_dump` / `ctx.dump` removal inventory omits two test files that reference the module attribute `rebar.mcp_server._dump` directly. `tests/unit/test_review_lifecycle_docs.py:36` and `tests/unit/test_gen_mcp_reference.py:124` each build a fake `ctx = SimpleNamespace(... dump=ms._dump ...)`. findings.checklist_item: State the back-out path for the breaking wire-shape change (e.g. 'revert is a single-commit no-data-migration rollback since no persisted state changes; canonical schemas are the only new artifact') or an expand-contract note, in the plan.
evidence: Approach: 'Null-vs-absent: a key the library omits is absent, never null.'
AC: 'docs/release-notes.md has the BREAKING entry stating the null-to-absent rule and naming the keys measured on the wire per tool family'
Rubric T4 remedy: 'an explicit ROLLBACK / back-out plan or expand-contract sequencing — checking only that breakage is acknowledged is insufficient'
findings.finding: The change flips the MCP wire contract from null-valued keys to absent keys (a consumer-observable breaking change) and deletes a module/env-var/config, but states no rollback / back-out mechanism — only a BREAKING release-notes entry, which the rubric treats as acknowledgement without reversibility.
findings.location: Approach ('Null-vs-absent: a key the library omits is absent, never null') and Acceptance Criteria (release-notes BREAKING entry)
scenarios: A downstream MCP consumer parses tool results expecting a `null` key (e.g. assignee/last_reopened_at) and now receives an absent key, breaking its deserializer with no documented revert path.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a one-line reversibility note to Approach/Scope: the cutover touches only in-process schema registration and return shapes (no persisted data), so back-out is a clean revert of the commit; confirm no consumer depends on the removed null keys before merge.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify how _wire_bytes/_bound_list_payload preserve accurate wire-size measurement once list tool bodies return raw library dicts instead of validated pydantic rows (the module's own docstrings say raw dicts under-estimate), and update test_mcp_list_read_surface.py's measurement oracle accordingly.
evidence: _mcp_budget.py:95-100 _wire_bytes docstring: 'Model defaults and quoted JS-unsafe integers enlarge reducer rows … Callers therefore pass post-validation rows'
_mcp_budget.py:113-117 _bound_list_payload: 'rows are the VALIDATED output models, not the raw reducer dicts -- see _wire_bytes for why sizing the raw dicts under-estimates the real payload'
tests/interfaces/facades/test_mcp_list_read_surface.py:323-325 records raw dicts 552,772 bytes vs after model_validate 1,526,327 bytes
Plan Approach: list tool bodies annotated '-> list[dict[str, Any]]' and 'return the library dict or list unchanged'
findings.finding: The plan removes the pydantic validation step from list read tools (bodies now 'return the library dict or list unchanged') but the budget consumer _bound_list_payload/_wire_bytes is documented to depend on receiving VALIDATED models because raw reducer dicts under-measure the real wire payload; the plan names _wire_bytes as an edit target without specifying how the response-size budget stays accurate against raw dicts.
findings.location: Approach — 'Tool bodies return the library dict or list unchanged' / 'Update _mcp_budget._wire_bytes'
scenarios: A large list_tickets result that was over-budget (and refused) under the validated-row measurement now measures ~1/3 the size as raw dicts and is emitted, exceeding the real token budget on the wire.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify that inline_schema rewrites any schema-local $id-relative self-ref ('<name>.schema.json#/...') to a bare JSON-pointer ('#/...') when it drops $id, so dropping $id never orphans an internal $defs ref in the new result schemas.
evidence: Plan: 'inline_schema(names, kind) hoists common.schema.json#/$defs/* into local $defs and drops $schema/$id (transitively; jsonschema.validate cannot resolve cross-file refs).'
Verified: non-advertised grounding.schema.json/terraform_*.schema.json already use self-$id refs ('grounding.schema.json#/$defs/...'), establishing the pattern a new advertised schema could follow.
test_output_schemas_are_self_contained would catch an orphaned ref at test time, but the plan does not direct the mechanism to handle it.
findings.finding: inline_schema's ref-rewrite spec pins dropping $schema/$id and transitively hoisting common.$defs, but does not state that a schema-LOCAL $id-relative self-ref (e.g. '<name>.schema.json#/$defs/foo') must be rewritten to a bare '#/$defs/foo' once $id is dropped. All currently-advertised schemas ref only common, so this is latent, but the new result schemas the plan adds (gate_run, verify_completion_status, write_ack, attach_commits_result) are exactly the kind that could grow an internal $defs, at which point dropping $id would orphan a now-unresolvable self-ref.
scenarios: A new advertised result schema is authored with an internal $defs and a '<self>.schema.json#/$defs/x' ref; inline_schema drops $id and the self-ref no longer resolves, failing validation at startup or in the self-contained test.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State in the plan whether `verify_completion_status.verdict` is a plain string or an enum; if enum, enumerate the full classifier vocabulary (certified, unsigned, stale-reopened, stale-material, not-closed, …) or keep it an open `type: string` to match the producer.
evidence: gate_runs.py:377-379 docstring: verdict is 'certified' only when valid now, else the classifier reason (stale-reopened / stale-material / not-closed / unsigned / …) — explicit ellipsis = open set
gate_runs.py:417 sets verdict = str(validity.get('verdict') or 'unsigned') — no closed enumeration at the producer
Current mirror _mcp_models.py:461 types it `verdict: str` (a bare open string), so advertising a closed enum would be strictly narrower than what the tool emits

The plan opens with 'the mirror is a second contract that can only be wrong' — the SAME over-constraint risk applies to an under-specified enum here (mcp/server/lowlevel/server.py validates every result against outputSchema)
findings.finding: The plan's new `verify_completion_status` schema names fields (`ok`, `verdict`, `reason`; nullable `verified_at_sha`, `signed_at`) but never states the value vocabulary of `verdict`, which is OPEN-ended at the source. If the author authors `verdict` as a closed enum, the advertised schema will reject valid wire payloads under jsonschema.validate.
findings.location: Approach — 'verify_completion_status (ok, verdict, reason; nullable verified_at_sha, signed_at)'
scenarios: A completion attestation is stale-material or not-closed; gate returns verdict='stale-material'; a closed-enum outputSchema fails validation and the tool call errors instead of returning the status.
findings.suggested_fix: Declare `verify_completion_status.verdict` as `{"type": "string"}` (open), matching the current `verdict: str` mirror and the open classifier reason set; do not pin a closed enum unless every compute_validity verdict is enumerated.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Pin `gate_run.status` as the closed enum {running, passed, failed, attaching, unknown} and declare `gate_run.verdict` as an open `type: string` (it includes daemon-stopped and gate-specific verdicts, not just pass/fail).
evidence: gate_runs.py:324-325 docstring: status is running / passed / failed / attaching / unknown (a bounded 5-value set)
gate_runs.py:311 materializes a stale run with verdict='daemon-stopped' — verdict is NOT limited to pass/fail
Current mirror _mcp_models.py:466-474 declares neither status nor verdict as enums (status: str; verdict absent, carried as permissive extra), i.e. the live wire shape is open on verdict
The plan asserts `wrap_output == (kind != 'object')` fails at startup for a mis-declared kind, so a mis-authored enum here is equally a startup/validation hazard
findings.finding: The plan's new `gate_run` schema lists `status` and optional `verdict` but does not pin their value vocabularies. `status` is a bounded 5-value set at the producer while `verdict` is open (includes `daemon-stopped` plus pass/fail), and the plan does not say which is a closed enum — leaving a startup-asserted outputSchema that could reject settled verdicts.
findings.location: Approach — 'gate_run (job_id, status; nullable ticket_id/gate_type; optional verdict/error/durable/findings)'
scenarios: A gate daemon stops and gate_status returns status='failed', verdict='daemon-stopped'; a closed verdict enum omitting daemon-stopped fails jsonschema.validate.
A follower polls before the leader writes an index record and status='attaching'; a status enum missing 'attaching' rejects the poll.
